day_shape: 66 items: Iran claims downing of US MQ-4C Triton over Bandar Abbas, Araghchi says Strait of Hormuz management will not revert, Houthi missile/drone salvoes intercepted over Riyadh and Mecca/Medina, IDF kills two Hamas/PIJ financiers in Gaza, nothing from UK Parliament or OFAC.

threads.label: Bandar Abbas drone and US posture
threads.summary: Defa Press and Tasnim claimed Iranian army air defence downed a US MQ-4C Triton drone over Bandar Abbas, while CENTCOM posted imagery of A-10 patrol flights over the Middle East. The Jerusalem Post relayed the Iranian army claim via Tasnim.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz and US pressure
threads.summary: Foreign Minister Araghchi said per Defa Press that Strait of Hormuz management will not revert to its prior state, while Iran International reported Tehran's envoy to Pakistan offered reopening if Washington lifted a naval blockade as Trump raised prospect of strikes. Defa Press also published commentaries on oil at $117 and the US 'Mother of All Bombs'.

threads.label: Iran retaliation threats and plots
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Tehran is threatening strikes on an expanded target list including civilian infrastructure, and cited two Iranian officials describing plots to target US diplomats. Parliament speaker Qalibaf told Defa Press Iran would deliver a response 'beyond imagination' to any encroachment.

threads.label: Houthi–Saudi missile exchanges
threads.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones and missiles over Riyadh and the south, and two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Mecca and Medina were intercepted as the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports. IRIB cited Al-Masira reporting Saudi airstrikes on Taiz and Amran provinces, and Houthi media reported Saudi strikes in Sanaa.

threads.label: IDF Gaza and West Bank operations
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Hamas cell commander Alaa Ibrahim Nimer Arshi and PIJ operative Karam Riyad Hassan Abu Butaihan, accused of transferring millions of shekels from Iran and Turkey to Hamas, and reported troops killed two further operatives crossing the Yellow Line. Over the weekend forces operated in ~40 areas and 400 locations in Judea and Samaria, arresting ~40 suspects, with three Hebron residents detained for online support of Friday's attack.

threads.label: Iraq spillover and Syria concerns
threads.summary: Iran International and the Jerusalem Post reported Baghdad believes Israel was behind recent strikes on Iran-backed militia weapons stockpiles in Iraq, with militias accusing the US of airspace violations amid disarmament tensions. A security source told Walla that Israel is concerned Syrian regime–linked operatives intend to renew attacks on Druze in southern Syria.

threads.label: Iran domestic pressures and judiciary
threads.summary: President Pezeshkian said many Iranians are struggling with US economic pressure and blamed Washington for interim-deal failure, while Iran International reported mobile data prices up to 40% higher and an uptick in Baluch attacks (18 in 18 days to 10 October). IRIB reported the Supreme Court upheld a 12-year sentence against Sadegh Saadi-Nia, and parliament obligated publication of a 'hostile media' list.

events.title_en: Axios: Crisis in US aviation; fuel and ticket price surge following war with Iran
events.summary_en: Axios: Crisis in US aviation; fuel and ticket price surge following war with Iran. The Axios news agency reported intensifying financial pressures on US airline companies due to the astronomical increase in fuel prices. The surge in fuel rates has caused a marked increase in ticket prices and the elimination of economy and budget flights for passengers. American Airlines reported a 70 per cent increase in fuel costs in the third quarter of 2026, bringing a new financial burden of nearly 2 billion dollars. United Airlines has reduced its annual profit forecast and Delta Airlines announced that this year's fuel costs are 6 billion dollars heavier than last year.

events.title_en: Amid protests, France restricts access to social media networks
events.summary_en: Amid protests, France restricts access to social media networks. French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu requested that four major telecommunications operators in the country be prepared for temporary suspension of public access to social media networks. This measure was presented following the 17 and 18 October protests and the unrest that followed. French officials claim that during these protests, virtual space platforms were used to coordinate violent actions, exchange information about targets and disseminate information about the movements of security forces.

events.title_en: Internet cables: an asymmetric and vulnerable target at the heart of digital interests
events.summary_en: Internet cables: an asymmetric and vulnerable target at the heart of digital interests. Submarine cables are the backbone of global financial communications and the data passing through these cables belongs to banks, energy companies, commercial platforms and government services. Disruption to them will disrupt financial transactions, e-commerce and cloud computing. The Strait of Hormuz has long been recognised as a vital artery for oil transmission; however, a less visible layer of this waterway is its role as one of the important nodes of global digital infrastructure. In the bed of this strait, at least seven main telecommunications cables are located carrying internet data, financial transactions and cloud services.

events.title_en: The 'Mother of All Bombs' in the continuation of America's psychological war against Iran
events.summary_en: The 'Mother of All Bombs' in the continuation of America's psychological war against Iran. The 'Mother of All Bombs' should be examined both as a weapon with specific military capabilities and as a subject in the field of strategic communications. The importance of the subject is not limited to the possibility of using this bomb. Media naming of this weapon, display of images of massive explosions and repetition of threats related to its use can create an image of widespread destructive power and unlimited military capability. In such an environment, the audience may, more than gaining information about the actual capability of the weapon, the type of target and operational limitations, be affected by the image that has been created of its power.
